skill.name: image-to-video
skill.description: Routes still-image animation requests to HappyHorse, Wan, or Seedance models through RunComfy, with model-specific prompts and media parameters.
skill.summary: Turn still images into short videos using intent-based model selection and RunComfy CLI guidance.
skill.author: genmedia-labs

security_audit.summary: All 67 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, documented CLI examples, URL placeholders, and a documented token path. The skill intentionally sends prompts and media references to RunComfy, creating a low-severity privacy consideration, but no malicious behavior or prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Prompts and referenced media are processed by RunComfy infrastructure.
remediation.suggestion: Request confirmation before submitting sensitive media, and direct users to RunComfy privacy, retention, and billing terms.

content.user_title: Animate Still Images with the Right Video Model
content.value_statement: Choosing an image-to-video model and its parameters can require repeated testing. This skill routes each request and provides focused RunComfy invocation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Classifies animation requests and selects HappyHorse, Wan, or Seedance based on the requested result.
Guides general portrait, product, and camera-motion animation with HappyHorse 1.0.
Configures Wan 2.7 for talking-head generation driven by a supplied voiceover.
Configures Seedance 2.0 Pro with image, video, and audio references.
Provides model-specific limits for duration, resolution, aspect ratio, file size, and reference count.
Builds RunComfy CLI guidance and downloads generated outputs to a chosen directory.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, an authenticated RunComfy account, and accessible media URLs.
Each request uses one model route; combining outputs from several routes requires separate processing.
Generated clips are limited to model-specific durations, resolutions, aspect ratios, and media sizes.
Prompts and media references are sent to RunComfy and may incur provider charges.

use_cases.title: Animate Product Photography
use_cases.description: Create a short product reveal with controlled camera movement while preserving packaging and geometry.

use_cases.title: Produce Localized Spokesperson Clips
use_cases.description: Generate consistent talking-head videos from separate voiceover tracks for different languages.

use_cases.title: Combine Creative References
use_cases.description: Use subject images, scene videos, and voice references to plan a multimodal short clip.

prompt_templates.title: Animate One Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate [image URL] for [duration]. Use one gentle motion, preserve the subject, and save the result to [output directory].
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a simple animation from one image.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Product Reveal
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn [product image URL] into a [duration]-second reveal. Use [camera motion], keep branding unchanged, and choose the best route.
prompt_templates.scenario: A designer needs controlled motion and stable product details.

prompt_templates.title: Lip-Sync a Voiceover
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [aspect ratio] spokesperson clip using [audio URL]. Match the duration, preserve visual consistency, and avoid subtitles, flicker, and distortion.
prompt_templates.scenario: A producer has a finished voice track for a talking-head clip.

prompt_templates.title: Direct a Multimodal Scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [image URLs] for identity, [video URLs] for scene motion, and [audio URLs] for voice. Specify reference roles and generate [duration] seconds.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user wants coordinated image, video, and audio references.

output_examples.input: Animate a portrait for five seconds with a slow camera drift and stable facial features.
output_examples.output: Selected HappyHorse 1.0 for identity-preserving portrait motion. Prepared a five-second prompt with gentle drift and stable facial details.

output_examples.input: Create a vertical spokesperson clip that follows my twelve-second English voiceover.
output_examples.output: Selected Wan 2.7 with the supplied voiceover. Matched a twelve-second duration and vertical aspect ratio for lip-sync.

output_examples.input: Use my character image, cafe reference clip, and voice sample to create an eight-second scene.
output_examples.output: Selected Seedance 2.0 Pro. Assigned the image to identity, video to scene motion, and audio to voice reference.

best_practices: Use one primary motion per clip and describe camera movement before secondary visual details.
State preservation goals clearly, including identity, packaging, costume, or background geometry.
Match duration to supplied audio and reuse a seed when comparing controlled variants.
anti_patterns: Do not restate every visible image detail when the prompt should describe change and motion.
Do not combine references with conflicting visual styles unless visible drift is acceptable.
Do not submit private media without reviewing RunComfy privacy, retention, and billing terms.

faq.question: Which model is used by default?
faq.answer: HappyHorse 1.0 is the default for general portrait, product, and still-image animation.

faq.question: Can I use my own voiceover?
faq.answer: Yes. The Wan 2.7 route accepts an audio URL and uses it to drive talking-head lip-sync.

faq.question: Can one request combine image, video, and audio references?
faq.answer: Yes. Seedance 2.0 Pro supports multiple image, video, and audio references within its documented limits.

faq.question: Does the skill work without a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: No. You need the RunComfy CLI and either an authenticated login or a RunComfy token.

faq.question: Where are generated videos stored?
faq.answer: The RunComfy CLI downloads generated outputs into the directory selected for the request.

faq.question: Does media stay on my computer?
faq.answer: No. Prompts and media URLs go to RunComfy, and its model servers fetch referenced media for processing.
